title: Region onboarding acceptance worksheet and failover guidelines
text:
Region onboarding acceptance worksheet and failover guidelines

description:
Working ticket to capture a repeatable acceptance worksheet and decision guidance for customer requests that require region availability or data residency guarantees. This artifact is intended to standardize intake answers, produce a numerical acceptance score, map required engineering/legal actions, and surface a recommended failover topology for contracts. Aim: reduce decision time from ~2 weeks to 48-72 hours for non-blocking enterprise requests.

acceptance_criteria:
Intake form fields finalized and published to the Sales/CS intake template
Numerical scoring rubric implemented in the triage spreadsheet and accessible to PM/Infra/Legal reviewers
Failover topology decision tree documented with at least three canonical patterns (single-region, geo-failover, dedicated fallback pool)
Minimum feasible contract language snippets for residency and failover obligations prepared for Legal review
Owners (PM, Infra SRE, Legal, Solutions Eng) assigned and SLA for decision set to 72 hours for standard requests

scoring_rubric:
Business impact (weight 30): ARR potential, retention risk, sales urgency
Residency strictness (weight 25): customer legal residency vs. preferred locality
Technical feasibility (weight 20): infra changes required, ops automation availability
Security & compliance risk (weight 15): export control, encryption/KMS needs, audit workload
Strategic fit & churn reduction (weight 10): accelerates product-market fit or strategic partnership

decision_workflow:
1) Sales/CS submits intake with required docs (jurisdiction, data flow diagrams, expected QPS, sample payloads). 2) PM performs initial scoring within 24 hours. 3) If score >= 70, trigger Fast-Track: Infra provides feasibility + cost delta within 48 hours and Legal drafts residency clause. 4) If score between 40-69, schedule cross-functional review meeting within 72 hours to surface blockers and mitigation. 5) If score <40, provide templated fallback options (regional disclaimers, encryption-at-rest guarantees) and delay commercial commitments until formal pilot. All decisions recorded in the worksheet and linked to the customer's account ticket.

risk_matrix:
Low: standard hosted with regional availability, no export/encryption constraints. Medium: requires KMS integration or minor routing policy changes; impacts provisioning timeline. High: requires on-prem or VPC-only deployment, full data residency legal covenant, or introduces cross-border export risks. Mitigations: add contract fallback language, propose Dedicated pool, or require Private deployment and higher pricing. Residual risks must be tracked and included in the enterprise contract handoff.

comments:
2026-03-01 - Aisha Patel: Created initial ticket and drafted goals. Attached intake form mockup. Need Infra feasibility estimate.
2026-03-03 - Marcus Lee: Met with Infra SREs. Fast-Track feasibility looks plausible for GCP regions; AWS has quota lead times. Added ENG-34012 for autoscaling template changes.
2026-03-05 - Priya Menon (Legal): Reviewed initial contract snippets. Raised question about subprocessor disclosures and if we can accept customer-specific audit clauses.
2026-03-07 - Marcus Lee: Updated scoring rubric weights based on Sales feedback; added revenue weight. Drafted three canonical failover topologies for review.
2026-03-09 - Solutions Eng (Jon Ramos): Ran sample QPS through simulated routing policy; latency meets SLO in single-region but inter-region failover adds tail-latency risk. Recommend TTL-based routing and warm standby pool.
2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel: Pulled together worksheet and linked to Sales intake. Next step: Legal to provide final clause options and Infra to estimate cost delta for Dedicated vs Private options. Target decision by 2026-03-21.
